title: wringer.judgement.v1
description:
`wringer.judgements.yaml` at the repository root — one entry per `human: true` criterion a PERSON has answered.

**A file a person edits, exactly like `approved: true` in `wringer.spec.yaml`, and for exactly the same reason.** There is deliberately no flag, no `--judge`, no `--accept-human` and no environment variable that writes an entry. Nothing in Wringer gives any model, agent or command the ability to answer a criterion a human was asked to answer: a `human: true` criterion exists precisely because a model asked anyway would be guessing, and a machine that could fill in its own answer would be the vibe tooling this project exists to answer.

A SIBLING file rather than a key on the criterion, because `wringer.spec.v1` is frozen and its criterion object is `additionalProperties: false` — an `answer:` key there would cost `wringer.spec.v2`, a version reaching the drafter, the approval interlock and `wring plan`, for a field none of them produce. The same shape `digests.json` and `briefed.json` already use.

**What a judgement does NOT pin, stated because it is the weak part.** It is not pinned to a tree, a commit, a bundle or a build. A person judged a running product at a moment; later work can break what they approved, and nothing here detects that. Pinning to the tree would invalidate every judgement on every commit — a constant-no wearing a rigour costume, and a refusal that always fires teaches people to route around it. The honest mechanism for 'the thing I approved has regressed' is the ratchet: the person says so, and the correction becomes a criterion with a check demonstrated red today.

judgements.description: One entry per criterion answered. A criterion with no entry is UNANSWERED, which is a state and not a judgement — absence is never read as 'met'.

criterion.description: The id of the criterion this answers. An id no approved spec declares is ignored rather than an error: a spec can be edited under a judgement file, and taking down a verification over a stale entry would be worse than skipping it.

verdict.description: **Two values, closed.** `met` or `not_met`. There is no `partially`, no score, and no third value that means 'probably' — a judgement that can hedge is a judgement nothing downstream can act on.

by.description: A free-text name. **Recorded, never verified.** This is not an identity system and nothing downstream may read it as one; `wring attest --sign` is where identity claims live, and this is not that.

at.description: ISO-8601. The person's own claim about when they answered — not observed, not checked, and not compared against anything.

criterion_digest.description:
sha256 of the criterion this answers, over the PARSED object: `{"id", "title", "guidance"}`, JSON with sorted keys, no ASCII escaping, tight separators. Parsed rather than raw bytes, so a whitespace- or comment-only edit to `wringer.spec.yaml` does not stale every judgement in the repository, and so an absent `guidance` and an empty one are already the same value before the digest sees them. `required` and `human` are deliberately EXCLUDED: changing either changes the policy, not the question, and a criterion that stops being required has not been reworded.

If the requirement IS reworded, every judgement of it goes stale and the row refuses again under `human-judgement-stale` — somebody answered a different question.

note.description: Optional free text. Rendered verbatim wherever it is rendered at all; never parsed and never routed on.
